c3dc93fb-8ac2-403a-902d-ee660379a7f5.objective: Design and document the complete architecture for a real-time notification system: define the Notification data model (schema, fields, types, delivery states, user associations), specify REST and WebSocket API contracts (endpoints, payloads, event schemas), and produce a frontend hook interface definition with module structure — all delivered as a standalone architecture document consumable by downstream Coder, Test, and Deployment agents.
requiredInputs: High-level requirements for the real-time notification system (notification types, delivery channels, user roles)
Target tech stack assumptions (e.g., Node.js/TypeScript backend, PostgreSQL or MongoDB, React frontend, WebSocket library such as Socket.io or native WS)
Authentication model context (e.g., JWT, session-based) to define user association strategy
Any existing data models or API conventions the new system must conform to

proposedSteps.action: Survey project context and establish stack assumptions
proposedSteps.detail: Inspect the workspace for any existing schema files, package.json, tsconfig.json, or README to infer tech stack, naming conventions, and database driver in use. If none found, document explicit assumptions (TypeScript, PostgreSQL via Prisma, Socket.io, React 18).

proposedSteps.action: Define the Notification data model schema
proposedSteps.detail: Draft the Notification entity with fields: id (UUID), userId (FK), type (enum: SYSTEM | ALERT | MESSAGE | PROMO), title, body, metadata (JSONB), status (enum: PENDING | DELIVERED | READ | FAILED), channel (enum: IN_APP | EMAIL | PUSH), createdAt, updatedAt, readAt (nullable), expiresAt (nullable). Define relationships to User and NotificationPreference tables.

proposedSteps.action: Specify delivery state machine and NotificationPreference model
proposedSteps.detail: Document the delivery state transitions (PENDING → DELIVERED → READ, PENDING → FAILED with retry policy) and define the NotificationPreference schema (userId, channel, enabled, quietHoursStart, quietHoursEnd) to support per-user delivery configuration.

Specify endpoints: GET /api/v1/notifications (paginated list, filters: status, type), GET /api/v1/notifications/:id, PATCH /api/v1/notifications/:id/read, PATCH /api/v1/notifications/read-all, DELETE /api/v1/notifications/:id, GET /api/v1/notifications/preferences, PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences. Document request/response payloads, HTTP status codes, and auth header requirements for each.

Specify Socket.io or WS event schemas: client emits subscribe_notifications {userId, token}, server emits notification:new {id, type, title, body, createdAt}, notification:updated {id, status}, notification:deleted {id}. Document namespace (/notifications), authentication handshake, reconnection strategy, and room-per-user pattern.

proposedSteps.action: Define frontend hook interface and module structure
proposedSteps.detail: Specify useNotifications() hook interface returning {notifications, unreadCount, isLoading, error, markAsRead(id), markAllRead, deleteNotification(id), preferences, updatePreferences(prefs)}. Define module structure: hooks/useNotifications.ts, hooks/useNotificationSocket.ts, components/NotificationBell.tsx, components/NotificationList.tsx, services/notificationApi.ts, types/notification.ts.

Compile all decisions into docs/architecture/notification-system.md with sections: Overview, Data Model (ERD description + field table), State Machine Diagram (ASCII), REST API Contract, WebSocket Contract, Frontend Module Structure, Hook Interface, Security Considerations, and Open Questions for downstream agents.

filesLikelyAffected.reason: Primary deliverable: the complete architecture document for downstream agents to consume
TypeScript type definitions and interfaces for the Notification, NotificationPreference, and related enums — machine-readable companion to the markdown doc
OpenAPI 3.0 YAML spec for all REST endpoints, enabling downstream Coder and Test agents to generate stubs and mocks
Dedicated WebSocket event schema documentation including payload examples and connection lifecycle
Describes the React module layout, hook interfaces, and service layer contracts for the frontend implementation agent
Add a section linking to the new architecture docs so all agents and collaborators can discover them

safetyChecks.check: No destructive database migrations or schema changes executed
safetyChecks.detail: This is a pure design/documentation step; no migration files are created or run, no database is touched.

safetyChecks.check: No hardcoded secrets or credentials in architecture documents
safetyChecks.detail: Architecture documents will use placeholder values (e.g., <JWT_SECRET>, <DB_URL>) and explicitly instruct downstream agents to source secrets from environment variables.

safetyChecks.check: Type safety verified in TypeScript interface definitions
safetyChecks.detail: The .ts definition file will be authored but not compiled at this stage; downstream Coder agent must validate it compiles against the actual project tsconfig. Enums and nullable fields need careful alignment with Prisma/ORM conventions.
All REST endpoints are scoped under /api/v1/ to prevent future breaking changes and align with common industry convention.

safetyChecks.check: Downstream agent dependency validity — no circular or missing dependencies
safetyChecks.detail: This agent has no dependencies and produces artifacts that all three downstream agents (Coder, Test, Deployment) depend on, forming a clean DAG.

risks.description: Stack assumptions made without confirmed project context could produce an architecture that conflicts with the actual tech stack (e.g., designing for Prisma/PostgreSQL when the project uses Mongoose/MongoDB)
risks.mitigation: Explicitly list all assumptions in the architecture document's 'Assumptions' section; downstream Coder agent must validate and flag any mismatches before implementation begins. Prefer database-agnostic field type descriptions with notes for both SQL and NoSQL variants.

risks.description: WebSocket contract may be ambiguous about authentication and reconnection behavior, causing the Coder agent to make incompatible implementation choices
risks.mitigation: Fully specify the authentication handshake (JWT passed as query param or in handshake auth object), reconnection backoff strategy, and what happens to queued notifications during disconnection in the WebSocket contract document.

risks.description: Frontend hook interface may not account for all edge cases (pagination, optimistic updates, offline support), leading to rework in the Coder agent phase
risks.mitigation: Include explicit notes on pagination cursor strategy, optimistic update patterns (rollback on failure), and a flag for whether offline queueing is in scope for v1 vs future iterations.

risks.description: OpenAPI YAML spec may contain inconsistencies with the TypeScript type definitions, causing Test agent to generate tests against a different contract than what is implemented
risks.mitigation: Cross-reference the OpenAPI spec and TypeScript interfaces during the document compilation step (Step 7); consider using a single source of truth approach where types are derived from the OpenAPI spec via code generation.

validationPlan.description: Manually review the Notification state machine for completeness: all PENDING → terminal state transitions are covered, no orphaned states exist
Lint the OpenAPI YAML spec using a tool such as Spectral or swagger-cli to catch structural errors, missing required fields, and undefined $ref references
Typecheck the TypeScript interface definition file (docs/architecture/notification-data-model.ts) in isolation using tsc --noEmit to verify syntactic correctness
Peer-review checklist: verify each REST endpoint has a documented error response (400, 401, 403, 404, 500), all WebSocket events have payload examples, and all hook return values are typed
Automated consistency check: parse the OpenAPI spec and the TypeScript types file to verify all response schema field names match between the two artifacts (simple script or CI lint rule)

a4a5cc73-e690-4ac8-8bcd-74faa78f9c22.objective: Implement a notification system consisting of: (1) backend REST endpoints for creating and retrieving notifications, (2) a WebSocket endpoint for real-time push delivery, (3) database models and migration scripts for the Notification schema with delivery states, and (4) a frontend React useNotifications hook that subscribes to the WebSocket and exposes notification state/actions — all strictly conforming to the architect's defined contracts.
requiredInputs: Completed Architect Agent output: Notification data model schema (fields, types, delivery state enum)
API contracts: REST endpoint signatures, request/response shapes, HTTP status codes
WebSocket event schema: event names, payload structures, connection/authentication protocol
useNotifications hook interface: exposed state shape, action signatures, subscription lifecycle
Database connection configuration (host, credentials, DB name) or environment variable conventions
Existing project structure to determine framework (e.g., Express/FastAPI/NestJS for backend, React version for frontend)
Authentication/authorization mechanism (e.g., JWT) for securing endpoints and WebSocket connections

proposedSteps.action: Read and internalize all architect contracts
proposedSteps.detail: Parse the architecture document to extract the Notification schema (id, userId, type, message, status, createdAt, readAt fields), delivery state enum (PENDING, DELIVERED, READ, FAILED), REST API contracts, WebSocket event schema (notification:new, notification:read, notification:error), and the useNotifications hook interface before writing any code.

proposedSteps.action: Create database model and migration for Notification schema
proposedSteps.detail: Create src/models/notification.ts (or .py/.js depending on stack) defining the Notification entity with all architect-specified fields and the DeliveryStatus enum. Generate a timestamped database migration file (e.g., migrations/20240101_create_notifications_table.ts) with up/down methods, adding indexes on userId and status columns.

proposedSteps.action: Implement the NotificationService with business logic
proposedSteps.detail: Create src/services/notificationService.ts implementing createNotification(), getNotificationsForUser(userId, pagination), markAsRead(notificationId, userId), and markAsDelivered() methods, each updating delivery states atomically and emitting WebSocket events on state transitions.

proposedSteps.action: Implement REST API controller and routes
proposedSteps.detail: Create src/controllers/notificationController.ts with handlers for POST /api/notifications (create), GET /api/notifications (list with userId filter and pagination), PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read (mark read), and wire them in src/routes/notificationRoutes.ts with authentication middleware applied to all routes.

proposedSteps.action: Implement WebSocket gateway/handler for real-time push
proposedSteps.detail: Create src/websockets/notificationGateway.ts that manages authenticated WebSocket connections keyed by userId, handles client subscribe/unsubscribe messages, and exposes a pushToUser(userId, event, payload) method used by NotificationService. Register the gateway in the application bootstrap.

proposedSteps.action: Implement the frontend useNotifications React hook
proposedSteps.detail: Create src/hooks/useNotifications.ts that on mount opens an authenticated WebSocket connection (using token from auth context), listens for notification:new and notification:read events to update local state, exposes { notifications, unreadCount, markAsRead, isConnected } per the architect's hook interface, and cleans up the connection on unmount.

proposedSteps.action: Wire everything together and run the migration
proposedSteps.detail: Register the notification routes and WebSocket gateway in the main application entry point (src/app.ts or main.ts), run the database migration in the development environment to verify it applies cleanly, and do a smoke test of each REST endpoint via curl/Postman and a manual WebSocket connection test.

filesLikelyAffected.reason: Defines the Notification entity class/interface and DeliveryStatus enum matching the architect's schema
Database migration to create the notifications table with all required columns and indexes
Business logic layer for CRUD operations on notifications and delivery state management
REST endpoint handlers conforming to the architect's API contracts
Route definitions wiring HTTP methods and paths to controller handlers with auth middleware
WebSocket connection manager and event emitter for real-time notification push
Frontend React hook implementing the architect's hook interface for consuming real-time notifications
Register notification routes and WebSocket gateway in the main application bootstrap

safetyChecks.check: No destructive or irreversible database migration
safetyChecks.detail: The migration creates a new table (safe), but if a notifications table already exists from a prior partial implementation, running the migration without checking could fail or silently conflict. A pre-migration check for table existence should be included in the up() method.

DB connection strings, JWT secrets, and WebSocket auth tokens must be sourced from environment variables (process.env). No secrets will be embedded in source files; .env.example will document required vars.

safetyChecks.check: Type safety verified across backend and frontend
safetyChecks.detail: Without seeing the architect's exact TypeScript types, there is a risk of interface drift between the backend response DTOs and the frontend hook's expected payload types. Shared type definitions should be extracted to a common types package or a shared file.

safetyChecks.check: WebSocket authentication enforced — no unauthenticated connections accepted
safetyChecks.detail: The gateway will validate JWT on the initial connection handshake and reject connections without a valid token, preventing unauthorized subscription to other users' notification streams.

safetyChecks.check: REST endpoints scoped to authenticated user — no IDOR vulnerability
safetyChecks.detail: All data access in the service layer will use the userId extracted from the validated JWT, never from the request body or URL params directly, preventing insecure direct object reference attacks.

risks.description: Architect's contracts are ambiguous or incomplete — missing fields, unclear delivery state transitions, or underspecified WebSocket event payload formats could cause misalignment with the Test Agent's expectations
risks.mitigation: Before coding, explicitly document assumptions about any gaps in the architecture document and surface them as questions. Codify all contracts as TypeScript interfaces in a shared contracts file that both backend and frontend import, making drift immediately visible at compile time.

risks.description: WebSocket connection management at scale — the in-memory userId-to-socket map in the gateway will not work in a multi-instance deployment
risks.mitigation: Implement the gateway with an adapter pattern (e.g., Socket.IO Redis adapter or similar pub/sub backend) so it is horizontally scalable from the start, even if only a single instance is used initially. Document this constraint clearly.

risks.description: Frontend hook WebSocket lifecycle issues — race conditions between component mount/unmount and async connection setup could cause memory leaks or duplicate event listeners
risks.mitigation: Use a useEffect cleanup function to close the WebSocket and remove all event listeners on unmount. Add a connection status guard to prevent state updates after unmount (using an isMounted ref or AbortController pattern).

risks.description: Database migration fails in the target environment due to insufficient permissions or conflicting schema from another developer's partial work
risks.mitigation: Include an idempotency guard (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) in the migration. Test the migration against a fresh database and a pre-populated database. Document the rollback (down) method thoroughly.

validationPlan.description: Run TypeScript compiler (tsc --noEmit) across backend and frontend to confirm zero type errors in all new files
Run ESLint with the project's ruleset on all created/modified files to enforce code style and catch common anti-patterns
Execute the database migration against a local test database and verify the notifications table schema matches the architect's data model using a schema introspection query

Send HTTP requests to each REST endpoint (POST /api/notifications, GET /api/notifications, PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read) with valid and invalid auth tokens to verify correct responses and status codes
Write and run a smoke integration test that creates a notification via REST, connects a WebSocket client with a valid token, and asserts the notification:new event is received within 500ms
